ambiguities: C07 (fixed or per draw): I fixed J and B1's pair J at the full sample; the top-k sets and their unions are found again on each draw; the determined signs come from the full bootstrap. Recomputed per draw, J would vary: defo feature 278-280, pm25 101-103 / 87-89, ndvi 477-479 / 94-96 (stored in active_set.extra). This changes the rank-statistic intervals.

C11 (top-20 union Spearman): I rank again within the union. This is often strongly negative because of the selection effect, while the full-sample value with ranks carried from J differs (stored in pairs.extra).

C15 (families): family shares exist only from variable-level phi, so the feature-level tv_family_shares is null. A family with no variable in the problem (coral own history, defo context and calendar) gets null rather than 0. Both are readings of 'the sum of its variables' (variable-level) phi'.
C16 (precedence): `calendar` passes the global-index data rule (the month is the same for every unit at a time step). Section 8 names calendar as context, and I gave the named families precedence.
C25: section 8 says 'For every arcsine-link model ... (fire)'. I covered coral's 4 arcsine models as well as fire's treeroute.

C22/C23 (median and range): ndvi has 4 rivals, so the median is the mean of the two middle values. I read 'the median rival' as the median of the rivals' own-history shares recomputed per draw, not as one fixed rival's share. The range ends get their own intervals.
C20: I read the stability as itself a mean over the draws, so it has no interval. C08: the counts recomputed per draw get intervals; n_J does not, because J is fixed.

C17: sign agreement is reported as the fraction n_agree / n_determined and is undefined when no player is determined in both models. C21: an interval is given whenever n_finite >= 1, which gives intervals from as few as 64 finite draws (fire ridge|treeroute).

I02: the protocol does not say which list of regions the draw integers index. I used sorted(group), which equals the first-appearance order in every problem; the integers themselves do not depend on region names.
I04: I took 'the lead's test set' to be the run's full lead-0 test export (all units and time steps) named in the rival SHAP log, not the 1,000 sampled rows.
surprises:
Each draw matrix is reproduced exactly, all 2000 x G entries in all 5 problems, as int.from_bytes(sha256('shap_v1|AW4|

|0||')[:8], 'big') mod G. per_lead's draws_sha256 covers the whole .npy file (header and data), not the data bytes alone.
Defo's B1 rows.parquet has the same file SHA-256 as the main run's; the identity is bit-exact.

Spearman over the top-20 union is often negative even where the overall agreement is high. pm25 has W 0.854 but a median union Spearman of -0.019. NDVI's minimum is -0.405 (ridge). Many coral feature-level pairs are negative. In the paper this could be misread as disagreement.
Coral's only structural zero is `normal`. Section 8's smoke map also lists 'four constant cyclone columns', but no cyclone column is constant in the registered sample.
Fire treeroute has only 8 determined signs at the feature level and 9 at the variable level, so 5 fire sign agreements are undefined. BARDL causes 3 more in ndvi.

Under B1 the seasonal normal dominates (it is exactly 0 under B2): its family share is 0.811 (fire), 0.703 (pm25) and 0.443 (ndvi), `normal` is B1's top variable in all three, and the main-vs-B1 family-share TV is 0.81, 0.70 and 0.49. Players exactly 0 in the main run enter the pair's J, among them c__ctx:month, the ndvi harmonics and pm25's conflict_events.
Fire treeroute has pre > 0 on only 226 of 1000 sampled rows, in 27 of 40 regions (the protocol says 75.4% of rows are 0; the sample has 77.4%).

Several full-sample RBO values sit at the edge of their percentile interval, for example pm25 RBO vs consensus 0.372 [0.365, 0.571] and defo 0.634 [0.613, 0.750]: near-ties at the top ranks flip across draws.

No row of any piece is S-RESID-flagged. My nonzero counts equal every meta.json's players_nonzero and variables_nonzero, B1 included. ndvi's x__epo_lag12 is missing for every unit at one test time step.
BARDL's stability rounds to 1.0000 because 470 of its 479 feature-level J players tie at 0.
